name: App install and update time
plain: Android gives exact install and update timestamps; iOS gives them only indirectly.
meaning: Install time pins when a person got an app, and (with install referrer) which campaign. Android values are exact to the millisecond.

ios.api_surface: Container timestamps are covered by the file timestamp Required Reason API

limits.headline: Can see when it was installed and last updated, with exact times on Android
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app starts up
can: Check the exact install and update times on Android
Estimate the install date on iPhone from file clues
Use this to tell new users from older ones
cannot: See install times for other apps
Get exact times on iPhone, where it is only indirect
limits.differs: Android gives exact install and update times. iPhone only gives it indirectly.

story.what_it_is: Apps can read the date and time they were installed and last updated.
story.for_you: You never see it. An app knows exactly when you got it. It can show how many days are left on a trial or tell which ad campaign brought you.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for trial timers and to match an install to an ad. The exact Android time helps join datasets and attribute installs.

use_cases.example: A streaming app counts down a seven day free trial from the install time.
A game gives a new player welcome rewards for the first three days.
An ad network matches an install time to a click to give credit to a campaign.
A product team measures how long people use the app after install.
A fraud tool flags a brand new install used for a big transfer.
A store gives a first order discount only to new installs.
A fitness app builds a 30 day plan starting from install.

risks: Reveals when you got an app
story.android_note: Android gives exact install and update times to the millisecond.
story.ios_note: iOS gives it only in indirect ways.

technical_bounds: iOS needs StoreKit 2 or file timestamps
